quotes.text: DAX is nothing without the model. And that's something that people struggle to understand at first.
quotes.speaker: Bernat Agulló Roselló
quotes.why: Names the most common misconception of DAX beginners in one sentence.

quotes.text: And it's not just the time itself. I would say it's also the mental health of your developers and you have to do boring stuff.
quotes.speaker: Bernat Agulló Roselló
quotes.why: Argues that BI automation pays off beyond saved hours by removing tedious work.

quotes.text: But when you really want exact values and you really want the truth, I think it's a very dangerous thing to put in between you and the answer is a black box
quotes.speaker: Bernat Agulló Roselló
quotes.why: A clear caution against relying on non-deterministic AI for exact business figures.

quotes.text: you're going to spend a lot of time in the community and so on. So you better enjoy it. And while you are doing something that you're enjoying, maybe there's some good things will come out of it.
quotes.speaker: Bernat Agulló Roselló
quotes.why: Honest advice on community work: do it for enjoyment, not for return on investment.

takeaways: DAX only makes sense together with the data model, so investing time in modeling fundamentals and the classic DAX books pays off early.
Tabular Editor with C# scripts, calculation groups and DAX user-defined functions removes repetitive model work and protects developers from error-prone copy-paste tasks.
Local user groups grow through steady activity, first-time and diverse speakers and annual sponsors, and community work is most rewarding when it is done for enjoyment.
hook: Many Power BI developers struggle with DAX, repetitive model maintenance and finding their place in the community. Microsoft MVP Bernat Agulló Roselló shares how Tabular Editor scripting, calculation groups and DAX UDFs automate semantic model work, and how BI professionals can grow through local user groups.
